contexts.text: Thus fly away with them, like a hawk with its prey under its wings.
A hawk flew up, and put his neck into the snare, and was caught; and the dove, seeing the hawk, flew past.
Their internal may be compared to a hawk, and their external to a dove; and the faith and charity of the latter to the flight of a hawk above a fleeing dove, which it at last tires out...
Like a hawk in a dovecot.
The natural man separated from the spiritual is like a hawk pursuing a dove.
